pins.en: Select the dashboards you want Loona to filter.
Choose Selected accounts or All accounts.
Home Assistant permissions always apply; Loona never grants or removes anyone's access.
Optionally install the Loona settings, Loona statistics and Loona benchmark cards.
Loona will create a Loona dashboard with those cards, visible to administrators only.
Pick none to skip this step.
Refresh your browser so the new dashboard card files load.
Turning it off resumes Home Assistant's normal behavior.
Your settings are kept as-is.
Sends only the entities your chosen dashboards use, plus any specific entities you added under Entity rules.
Trims the entity, device, area, floor and label lists.
Live updates for current tab only
Hidden tabs will not update until you view them.
After the first load, only the tab you are viewing keeps updating.
Prevents loading the card files that none of your dashboards actually use.
Reload your dashboard after changing this.
Delays building graphs that are off-screen until the rest of the page has settled.
Scrolling a graph into view loads it right away.
After a period of no activity, the dashboard stops live updates and refreshes its values only at a set interval, until any interaction brings live updates back.
You can set the Idle after time and the Idle refresh interval.
Briefly pauses repeating animations while the dashboard starts up, then resumes them.
Pauses repeating animations on cards that are scrolled out of view and resumes them when you scroll back.
Starts downloading the current tab's card files before Home Assistant requests them.
This does not change when they run.
Delays other tabs' card files until the current tab has rendered, then loads them gradually.
Opening a pop-up, switching tabs or pages, or editing loads the remaining files right away.
Editing a dashboard normally triggers this automatically; press this button to force a rescan now.
Your Loona settings and Home Assistant's recorded history are untouched.
Clears the live counters, recent page-load records and browser readings.
Restores Loona back to default settings, as if you had installed it fresh.
Also removes the Loona dashboard (if you have not edited it).
You will need to select dashboards and accounts again before filtering resumes.
An edited Loona dashboard, Loona cards you placed yourself, and recorded history are kept.
What gets sent to the dashboard is only what your selected dashboards actually use, plus whatever you add under Entity rules.
Person, update and zone entities cannot be excluded, because the Home Assistant interface needs them.
You can add single entities, a whole entity type (like sensor or light), or patterns such as sensor.kitchen_*, which means every sensor whose name starts with kitchen_.
The Excluded list takes precedence over Included.
Loona cannot always correctly guess every entity a custom card or pop-up requires.
Selecting Skip unused card files will load only the card files your dashboards need.
Always reload the dashboard after you make a change.
Opening a tab, opening a pop-up, or editing a dashboard refreshes values right away.
This affects ordinary live connections only - cameras, independent clocks, card timers and raw event listeners will keep going.
Changes in between are not displayed.
At 0, values remain frozen until you interact.
It describes potential entity reduction, not measured update reduction, and remains visible when filtering is off.
It does not measure loading time.
These reports cover only part of the browser's work.
A live connection is the link a dashboard tab keeps open to Home Assistant.
These figures measure entity updates, not data size, bandwidth, CPU usage or loading speed.
Chart history is kept only in memory and clears on reset or restart.
Safari and the Home Assistant Companion app for iOS and macOS use WebKit, which may not report decoded file sizes for cached scripts, even when the files loaded successfully.
After the benchmark ends, Loona tries to recover the missing file sizes using cache-only reads.
If any pass still lacks a file size, Card files loaded instead compares file counts for both modes.
Chrome and Edge 123+ support it; Firefox, Safari and the iOS and macOS Companion apps (WebKit) do not.
The benchmark measures reloads with the browser cache, not cold-cache loads or a guaranteed hard refresh.
Readiness waits for visible cards and icons to render, visible images and fonts to load, and pending native requests to finish.
Cameras, charts and custom content may still be loading.
File sizes cover observed registered resource entry files, not every imported dependency.
Idle savings only appear if the configured idle threshold is reached.
Cross-origin restrictions can also hide sizes.
Share of updates filtered out
Look at the optional files under Card files and at the Home Assistant log.
Missing entity IDs alone do not cause this.
